member_handoff.notes: transport.json currently holds 2 records and uses text names, not place IDs. Member 3 owns that file and should reference these IDs.

A road-distance file or field was not created because it would break the same-format rule.
Addresses and PIN codes of the 4 market and restaurant records remain unchecked.
Coordinates of 15 records remain without a map check.
All source links still need to be opened manually.
heritage.json (Member 1), transport.json (Member 3), and visitor_services.json (Member 4) were not changed.

Prepared 2026-10-23. Every statement below is marked as checked, or as not checked.
1. Result in one view
The dataset has 19 places (monument 7, religious 4, nature 2, market 2, garden 2, restaurant 2). 11 are original
records and 8 were added. No original record was changed. No duplicate exists. Each record has exactly the 7 fields:
id, name, category, latitude, longitude, address, source_url. The file is sorted by id. The file has no distance field,
because the backend computes distance_km.
Test results. Member 2 reported all tests passing on their own machine (134 tests, run on 2026-10-23, before the final
JSON update). The check script prints OK: 19 places, no duplicates or broken ids. The tests should be run once more
after the final JSON is copied in.

5. Straight-line distance and road distance from the Taj Mahal
Straight-line = the shortest distance over the ground between two points, computed by the haversine formula from the
coordinates in the JSON. The API uses the same formula for distance_km. Road distance = the distance a vehicle
travels. It is always longer. The road column below is only an estimate: straight-line x 1.2 to x 1.5 for city roads, x 1.1
